gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly identifies the false implication that a minimizer under the projected-mass constraint can be rescaled into the standard L2-constrained minimizer. It distinguishes the two Rayleigh quotients and explains that their minimizing directions generally differ.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries identify the invalid rescaling argument: projected-mass minimization of E(v)/||P_Hv||² does not generally have the same minimizing ray as standard L2 minimization of E(v)/||v||², so scalar normalization cannot establish the claimed standard LOD minimizer.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed scalar-rescaling implication from the projected-mass-constrained minimizer to the standard L2-constrained LOD minimizer is false because the two Rayleigh quotients can have different minimizing directions.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the projected constraint and quotient, contrasts it with the standard L2 quotient, and explicitly explains that rescaling cannot convert between minimizers when the minimizing rays differ.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 concerns whether optimally selected step sizes lie in the small admissible interval required by the convergence theorem. It does not identify the specific missing absorption condition 4τ₀²E(u⁰)<1, equivalently τ₀²<(4E(u⁰))⁻¹, needed to replace the quartic error term by a quadratic one in lemma:Rnorm.
